_readme: Mythic pick schedule (mythic map, ticket 03) -- the PARALLEL AXIS table beside
class_choice_schedule.json. Same schema, same resolver (generic_func.levels_for with
schedule_attr='mythic_schedule'), but the key space is TIER, not class level: the tier is
passed where a class level would be. A second axis file, not a sixth convention.
Deliberately NOT a row inside class_choice_schedule.json: class_entry_for and
validate_class_choices.py's ast-parsed call-site gate both assume the roster of 68 rollable
classes, and a pseudo-class row would need carve-outs in each. This table's gate is
Tiers cap at 10 (RAW; resolve_mythic_tier clamps), so the compact rules need no ceiling --
the same reason the class table dropped `until`. What a tier above 10 would even mean is the
map's 'Mythic above 20th' open question, not this file's.
The single 'class' key is `mythic`: one schedule for every path, because RAW grants every
path the same cadence -- the PATHS differ in their ability pools
Bucket keys are the names the code actually writes into data_dict['class features'] (the
sorcerer-row precedent in the class table): 'Mythic Path' and 'Mythic Path Abilities' are
sheet-visible section names; mythic_feats never reaches class features (it rides the general
feat track), so it keeps a code-shaped key.

Mythic Path.note: The path choice itself: one of the six RAW paths, picked once at tier 1 (v1 walks exactly one path -- Dual/Hard Path are recorded not-v1). Declared here on the same complete-inventory principle that put all 14 single-pick buckets in the class table.

Mythic Path Abilities.note: One path ability per tier (Mythic Adventures). The pool is the chosen path's, with the universal list merged in at build time -- one pool per path, one bucket on the sheet. Stamps carry the TIER, owner 'mythic'.

mythic_feats.note: One mythic feat at tier 1 and every second tier after (1,3,5,7,9). A separate allowance, never an ordinary feat slot: the grants are appended after the feat-count guarantee, profession-feat style, so the cap neither counts nor trims them.
